fields.statement:
Fix a system $s$ as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. A material constitution $c$ specifies a finite ordered list of named species $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$, with $r\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and $r\ge1$, and the model parameters that identify the material. An equilibrium-preparation label in the set $E_c$ selects a single macrostate that the model designates as an equilibrium state for constitution $c$. The equilibrium designation is primitive model input here; it is not a dynamical equilibration theorem or a global-stability claim. For each admitted preparation, its mechanical model supplies a positive total mass and a defined center-of-mass velocity as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], so the allowed boost can select a center-of-mass rest chart in which its internal energy is recorded. A preparation for which these mechanical data are unavailable lies outside this framework. A statistical preparation that instead supplies a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space is as in [[def-probability-measure]] and belongs to a separate statistical branch; it is an element of $E_c$ only if that model also assigns it a single equilibrium macrostate.

Each $e\in E_c$ is assigned a unique coordinate tuple $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, where $U$ is the adopted internal-energy coordinate in joules as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], $V>0$ is volume in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ is an amount in moles; the SI unit assignments are those of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. These are real-valued mole amounts in the bulk continuous chart, not integer particle counts. Define the dimensionless numerical coordinates $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$, $\hat V=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$, and $\hat n_j=n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. The representation map $\pi_c:E_c\to\mathbb R^{r+2}$ is a function as in [[def-function]], sends $e$ to $(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)$, and the equilibrium state domain is its image $D_c:=\pi_c(E_c)\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ using inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, write $U_c(x):=\hat U\,\mathrm J$, $V_c(x):=\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3}$, and $n_{c,j}(x):=\hat n_j\,\mathrm{mol}$ for its dimensioned coordinates. Preparation labels with the same coordinate tuple represent the same thermodynamic state in this framework. Statistical preparations that specify a probability law belong to a separate branch and are not used in this state-domain definition.

For fixed $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ in a chart used by the model, write $\Gamma_{c,n}=\{(\hat U,\hat V):(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)\in D_c\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, with inclusion notation as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. This designated slice is a specified nonempty open convex subset. With the dimensionless Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (a norm by [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), openness means that every $z\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ has some $\epsilon>0$ for which $\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\|w-z\|_2<\epsilon\}\subseteq\Gamma_{c,n}$. Convexity means that $(1-t)z_0+tz_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ whenever $z_0,z_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Both properties are assumptions about the particular slice, not conclusions about every $D_c$; no coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable merely because it lies in an ambient Euclidean space. A zero amount for an absent species belongs only to a separately specified boundary domain and is not in this positive-mole chart.

In a simple-compressible chart, volume $V$ is the only mechanical coordinate in the equilibrium representation; composition changes, fields, polarization, surface terms, and other mechanical coordinates require a separately declared state domain and exchange rules. No pressure or reversible-work formula follows from this definition.

For a system $s$ of constitution $c$, the process model fixes one Galilean inertial chart $g_s$ for kinetic-energy bookkeeping and transfer records and holds that chart fixed throughout each process. A process record is a tuple
$$P=(I_P,x_P^-,x_P^+,z_P,\kappa_P,r_P).$$
For each finite closed time interval $I_P=[t_0,t_1]\subseteq\mathbb R$ with $t_0<t_1$ as in [[def-interval]], measured in seconds, its component fields have these types: $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$ are equilibrium endpoint coordinates from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]; $Z_s$ is the model-declared configuration space of the system, its auxiliaries and devices; $Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq Z_s$ is the model-declared set of equilibrium configurations and $\xi_s:Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_c$ assigns their state coordinates; $z_P:I_P\to Z_s$ is a function ([[def-function]]); $\mathcal K_s$ is the model-declared set of control/contact records and $\kappa_P\in\mathcal K_s$; and $\mathcal R_s$ is the model-declared set of signed transfer records and $r_P\in\mathcal R_s$. These fields form a finite Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]]). The admitted records $\mathcal P_s$ are the model-specified subset of tuples with these types that additionally satisfy $z_P(t_0),z_P(t_1)\in Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}$, $\xi_s(z_P(t_0))=x_P^-$, and $\xi_s(z_P(t_1))=x_P^+$. No continuity or differentiability is imposed on $z_P$, and its values at interior times need not represent equilibrium states.

For an endpoint bookkeeping quantity $F$, write $\Delta F=F_P^+-F_P^-$. A closed record in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] has no matter crossing the chosen outer boundary. The core closed-record class $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\subseteq\mathcal P_s$ ([[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]) contains only records for which the system has a supplied total mass $M>0$ and defined center-of-mass velocities at both endpoints in the fixed chart $g_s$, so the kinetic energies $K_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm\|_2^2$ are defined as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. It further requires $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$, where $U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ denotes any model-specified external-field potential energy tracked separately from the internal-energy coordinate in $g_s$. Other process classes require an expanded energy bookkeeping rule.

For each $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$, the protocol supplies maps $Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}:\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\to\mathbb R$ whose values are interpreted in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]] and whose energy bookkeeping uses $g_s$. $Q[P]>0$ means energy enters the system through the declared thermal-transfer channel; $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]>0$ means mechanical work is done on the system. These are functionals of the process record, not state functions of $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$. Heat is the protocol-assigned thermal mode of energy transfer, not a quantity stored in the equilibrium state. A record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$. A closed record may still exchange energy; it is not thereby isolated.

A preparation is a model-specified rule selecting the particular initial equilibrium state $x_P^-$. A statistical extension may instead specify a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space, as in [[def-probability-measure]]; such a statistical preparation is outside this deterministic process class. A preparation does not assert later equilibration. An admitted record may pass through nonequilibrium configurations even though both endpoints lie in $D_c$.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. Fix their material constitutions $c_A,c_B$, each with a finite ordered list of distinct species labels as in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Fix an ordering $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$ of the labels occurring in either list, each occurring once, and use this as the species list of the compound constitution $c_{A\sqcup B}$. For $s\in\{A,B,A\sqcup B\}$, write $D_s:=D_{c_s}$ and use $U_s,V_s$ for its dimensioned coordinate maps. For every $1\le j\le r$, define the aligned amount map $a_{s,j}:D_s\to[0,\infty)\,\mathrm{mol}$ by $a_{s,j}(x):=n_{c_s,k}(x)$ if $\sigma_j$ is the $k$-th species in $c_s$'s list, and $a_{s,j}(x):=0\,\mathrm{mol}$ if it is absent. Distinctness makes $k$ unique. The absent-species value is a bookkeeping map on the existing $D_s$; it does not insert a zero coordinate into that constitution's positive-mole chart or assert a boundary-state extension.

The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. Adopt a composition function $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ ([[def-function]]) such that, for every $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$ and every $1\le j\le r$, its output satisfies
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad a_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=a_{A,j}(x_A)+a_{B,j}(x_B).$$
All quantities have the SI units of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. Each union species is present in at least one constituent with positive amount, so the summed amount is positive and agrees with the compound's $j$-th coordinate. The existence of an output in the declared $D_{A\sqcup B}$ is part of the adopted model, not a consequence of positivity.

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ with the same ordered species list and SI coordinate conventions as $c$, and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. The tag matters: $c^{(\lambda)}$ is not silently identified with $c$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

For each material constitution $c$, let $D_c$ be the equilibrium state domain from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. A **thermal-contact family** is a model-declared set $\mathcal T$ of tagged pairs $a=(c_A,x_A)$ with $x_A\in D_{c_A}$. Its tag and coordinate projections are $\operatorname{tag}(a)=c_A$ and $\operatorname{coord}(a)=x_A$; equal numerical coordinate tuples with different constitution tags are not identified.

Fix two members $a=(c_A,x_A)$ and $b=(c_B,x_B)$, named constituents $A,B$ of those constitutions, and a declared contact-protocol convention. A **thermal-contact protocol** is an admitted preparation/process record $P$ of their compound system $A\sqcup B$, with the configuration curve $z_P:I_P\to Z_{A\sqcup B}$ and equilibrium endpoint configurations specified in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The contact model supplies constituent endpoint-coordinate maps

$$\xi_A:Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_{c_A},\qquad \xi_B:Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_{c_B},$$

and requires $\xi_A(z_P(t_0))=x_A$ and $\xi_B(z_P(t_0))=x_B$. These constituent maps are additional declared model data; they are not inferred from the compound's coordinate tuple. Write $x_A^+=\xi_A(z_P(t_1))$ and $x_B^+=\xi_B(z_P(t_1))$ for the constituent final coordinates. The two constituents are separated by a declared diathermal contact: matter transfer and mechanical or composition work across that contact are forbidden, while the protocol permits thermal energy transfer between the constituents. The compound's external boundary and all retained constraints are specified as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] and [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. No continuity or differentiability of the configuration curve is added here.

The pair is in **thermal contact equilibrium**, written $a\sim_T b$, when, under that declared protocol convention, its admitted contact preparation has $x_A^+=x_A$ and $x_B^+=x_B$, is an equilibrium preparation, and permits no net heat transfer between the constituents. This criterion is protocol-dependent: changing the admitted contact preparation or retained constraints can change the relation. For fixed constitutions, coordinate notation $x_A\sim_T x_B$ abbreviates $(c_A,x_A)\sim_T(c_B,x_B)$ using the two specified tag embeddings. It does not define a relation on untagged coordinates across unspecified material types. The relation is defined only on the stated family $\mathcal T$ and for the declared contact protocols. This definition does not assert that $\sim_T$ is reflexive, symmetric, or transitive, and it does not assign a real-valued temperature to its equivalence classes.

A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types and a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each type. Each state set comes with a fixed formal composition $\nu_\Gamma$, and its states satisfy $\nu(x)=\nu_\Gamma$ as in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. These mathematical coefficients and their positive type weights are distinct from dimensioned material amounts. For physical channels the model additionally supplies endpoint quantity maps $U_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $n_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ in a declared finite species list, together with any separately tracked mechanical or external-field endpoint quantities. No identification of two distinct scaled tags is made.

For each channel $\alpha$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$, the model supplies sets $Z_\alpha$ of configurations, $\mathcal K_\alpha$ of protocol records, $\mathcal B_\alpha$ of outer-boundary records, and $\mathcal R_\alpha$ of transfer records, and equilibrium subsets and endpoint maps $\xi^-_\alpha:Z^-_\alpha\to X_\Gamma$, $\xi^+_\alpha:Z^+_\alpha\to X_{\Gamma'}$. A typed record is
$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. Transfer maps $Q_\alpha,W_{\mathrm{on},\alpha}:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $N_\alpha:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ record heat, work and material transfer with declared signs; any tracked $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are also joule-valued record maps. The channel specifies a balance predicate on this typed record set, or equivalently a balance map into a declared product of quantity spaces whose required value is zero, and a model-admitted subset satisfying that predicate. The predicate states the actual energy and material constraints of that channel; no balance law, physical admission or endpoint realizability follows from the tuple alone. For a fixed-constitution core closed channel, its endpoint embeddings, fields and admitted subset are exactly those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with no material transfer and its stated kinetic/external restrictions. Other channels require their own adopted constraints. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when an admitted channel record has those endpoints. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In this network class, explicitly adopt the represented state-family conditions of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. Each $X_T$ is a nonempty set of finite coefficient-map states with its declared fixed $\nu_T$. The separated-product map

$$\pi_{T,T\prime}:X_T\times X_{T\prime}\to X_{T\times T\prime},\qquad \pi_{T,T\prime}(a,b)=a+b$$

is surjective, so each admitted separated-product state has a factorization, which need not be unique. For every $t>0$, the positive coefficient-scaling map $s_{t,T}:X_T\to X_{tT}$, $s_{t,T}(a)=ta$, is a bijection with inverse scaling by $1/t$. These maps commute with the declared reassociation, permutation and scaling conventions and preserve the exact amount-function and formal-mass identities. The empty unit has $X_1=\{0\}$ with the empty coefficient map $0$. A chosen finite real baseline entropy family used for the chain costs must obey

$$\sigma_{T\times T\prime}(a+b)=\sigma_T(a)+\sigma_{T\prime}(b),\qquad \sigma_{tT}(ta)=t\sigma_T(a),\qquad \sigma_1(0)=0,$$

independently of a nonunique factorization. These are explicit admissibility and calibration conditions of the declared model, not consequences of a channel record or claims that every physical network satisfies them. Separated products remain sums of represented states; the distinct raw tags of scaled and joined types are retained, with reversible preparation transport as specified in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], rather than identifying those tags. The dimensioned endpoint-quantity maps and channel balance predicates remain the separately supplied physical data. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. A decorated finite chain is exactly a finite sequence of such allowed transitions with a common catalyst and the real baseline-entropy edge costs in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]].

For $\Gamma,\Gamma'$, let $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the infimum of those finite decorated-chain costs, with $+\infty$ if no witness exists and $-\infty$ if costs are unbounded below. The network has **no sinks** when, for every ordered type pair,

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a smooth $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and $H\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, with Hamiltonian field defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. Wherever its local flow $\phi_t$ is defined, it preserves the symplectic form and the volume measure $m$ determined by $\omega^n/n!$. No completeness is asserted. Let $R$ be a measurable region on which a nonzero-time map $T=\phi_\tau$ is defined and is forward invariant, $T(R)\subseteq R$. The restriction $T:R\to R$ preserves $m|_R$ if $T(R)=R$, or more generally if $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$. This latter condition holds automatically when $m(R)<\infty$. Thus for every finite-measure forward-invariant $R$ and every measurable $E\subseteq R$, almost every point of $E$ returns to $E$ infinitely often under forward iteration. Mere forward invariance of an infinite-volume region does not imply relative measure preservation.

If $m(R)=1$ and $T$ is ergodic, then for every $f\in L^1(R,m)$ the averages $N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}f(T^jx)$ converge almost everywhere and in $L^1$ to $\int_Rf\,dm$. Without ergodicity, the limit is the invariant conditional expectation supplied by Birkhoff's theorem, not necessarily the space mean. Finally, fix any real scalar $k_B$. If each stated time map $\phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism of a finite invariant region $R$, a density $p_0\ge0$ with $\int_Rp_0\,dm=1$ and $\int_R|p_0\log p_0|\,dm<\infty$ transports by $p_t=p_0\circ\phi_{-t}$ with conserved fine-grained entropy $-k_B\int_Rp_t\log p_t\,dm$, using $0\log0=0$. Volume preservation alone does not imply ergodicity or a time-average/ensemble identity.
fields.proof:
**Given:** [A1]–[A3] and the inspected supplier interfaces [F1]–[F6].

1.1 By [F1], $\omega$ is closed and $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. The Hamiltonian-flow theorem [F2], under its local existence domain, gives $\phi_t^*\omega=\omega$ and hence $\phi_t^*(\omega^n/n!)=\omega^n/n!$. The volume measure defined by this positive form is therefore preserved by each local flow diffeomorphism on its domain. For a measurable $E\subseteq R$, injectivity and volume preservation give $m((T|_R)^{-1}E)=m(E\cap T(R))$. If $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$, this equals $m(E)$, so the restriction is the measure-preserving system of [F3]. When $m(R)<\infty$, volume preservation gives $m(T(R))=m(R)$; because $T(R)\subseteq R$, finite additivity gives $m(R\setminus T(R))=0$. Thus the finite forward-invariant case follows without an onto hypothesis. Also $dH(X_H)=\omega(X_H,X_H)=0$ because a two-form is alternating, so each defined orbit stays on its energy level. This argument grants no flow outside its domain. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F3] to $p_t=p_0\circ\phi_{-t}$. It preserves $\int p_t\,dm=\int p_0\,dm=1$. The scalar function $u\mapsto u\log u$, defined to be $0$ at $u=0$ by [A3], is Borel; its absolute integrability is preserved because the same measure-preserving substitution gives $$\int_R|p_t\log p_t|\,dm=\int_R|p_0\log p_0|\,dm<\infty.$$ Applying integral invariance to its positive and negative parts proves $\int_Rp_t\log p_t\,dm=\int_Rp_0\log p_0\,dm$. Multiplication by the fixed real scalar $-k_B$ gives the stated scaled entropy conservation. [A2, A3, F3, F6, step 1.1]

2.2 The map $T$ on $R$ is measure preserving by 1.1 and [A2]. Its total measure is finite, so [F4] gives infinite returns for almost every point in each measurable $E\subseteq R$. The conclusion is explicitly almost everywhere and applies to the sampled map at the specified $\tau$. [A2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Under the additional probability and ergodicity assumptions in [A2], the hypotheses of [F5] hold for each $f\in L^1(R,m)$. Birkhoff therefore gives almost-everywhere and $L^1$ convergence to the invariant conditional expectation, and its ergodic corollary identifies that limit with $\int_R f\,dm$. If ergodicity is removed, only the invariant conditional expectation conclusion remains. Neither [F2] nor recurrence [F4] supplies ergodicity. [A2, F5, step 1.1] ∎

fields.statement:
Let $\mathcal G\ne\varnothing$ be a finite-factor-closed network of [[def-td-cross-type-reaction-network]]. Assume the contact hypotheses of [[pthm-td-entropy-under-product-comparison]] provide a finite real baseline entropy $\sigma_\Gamma$ on each type. Also assume that network satisfies A1–A6, its exact decorated-chain cost $F$ has the no-sinks property defined there, and the Axiom of Choice. Then there is a real offset $B(\Gamma)$ for each type, additive under finite composition and extensive under every positive scaling, such that the corrected entropy

$$S_\Gamma(x):=\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)$$

is nondecreasing across every admitted channel transition: if $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$, then $S_\Gamma(x)\le S_{\Gamma'}(y)$. The conclusion is weak monotonicity only. It does not assert a no-gap identity, uniqueness of $B$, strict increase, or a global entropy principle for networks that fail the stated hypotheses.
fields.proof:
**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F4].

1.1 Fix an admitted transition $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$. [F1] supplies finite baseline state values on both endpoint types, and [F2] supplies the surjective product maps, positive scaling bijections, zero unit and baseline compatibility required by the exact decorated-chain definition, and identifies its cost convention for this pair. Use the composition-preserving type-weighted representation from [F1]'s construction: interpret each encoded coefficient by its amount divided by the positive type weight, keeping the raw scaled and joined tags distinct. The network compares equal formal masses, and this interpretation preserves its admitted endpoint relation and each finite baseline entropy sum; hence each physical finite-chain witness and its coefficient-map image have the same real edge costs. Reversible regrouping of factors uses the adopted reversible-splitting axiom in [F2], so it changes neither the represented endpoints nor their baseline values. The cost $F$ used by [F3] is therefore this exact witness infimum, not one inferred from coordinate equality. Applying [F3] to this exact transition gives $$ \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)\ge F(\Gamma,\Gamma'). $$ If the edge exists, the one-edge chain makes $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty$, so this inequality has an ordinary real right side under the stated no-sinks hypothesis. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 The network’s no-sinks condition and [A1] match the hypotheses of [F4]; its cost is the same $F$ as in step 1.1 by [F2] and [F3]. Thus [F4] supplies one offset function $B$, common to all types, with additivity, positive-scale extensivity and $B(\Gamma)-B(\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ for every pair. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Subtract the bound in step 2.1 from that in step 1.1: $$ [\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)+B(\Gamma')]-[\sigma_\Gamma(x)+B(\Gamma)]\ge0. $$ By the definition of $S$ in the Statement, this is $S_{\Gamma'}(y)\ge S_\Gamma(x)$. The same $B$ works for every admitted transition, proving the conditional weak entropy principle. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
